title: Provenance frontmatter carried by every knowledge slice
description: Written by the assembler, never by hand. It is what makes a claim auditable back to its sources — including which agent, host, project and working copy produced them, and including after the observation store has been archived and emptied.

topic.description: The topic (the memory's file name) this slice file belongs to, written by the assembler on every file of the directory shape and of shared/: a budget part `<topic>-<n>.md` and a separate topic named `<topic>-<n>` have the same file name, and this is what tells them apart. A flat class file records its one topic too (a second topic moves the class into its directory); absent from a flat class file written before 2026-10-24, which may hold several topics, and from slices written before 2026-09-26.

description.description: One line, written as a retrieval cue: it becomes this slice's line in the role INDEX, which is the only thing a session sees before deciding to read further.

tier.description: 1 = loaded at role activation; 2 = loaded on demand via the index.

derived_from.description: Observation content hashes. Never local ids: those are per-database autoincrements that collide across hosts.

origin.description: Who produced the evidence and where: the agent (Linux login), the host, the logical project and the working-copy label, kept as separate facts. Records written by the retired clone-bound system carry `clone_id` instead of `agent` and are preserved verbatim as historical provenance (the project's .agent-fabric/legacy-registry/agent-map.json resolves them).

collisions.description: Titles that collided in this slice and were kept as '(N)' rather than replaced. The assembler writes it so the warning is a fact the file states — surviving drains that admit nothing for this slice — rather than something inferred from heading shapes, which an authored document may legitimately match.

translates.description: A locale translation of an authored identity file: the repo-relative path of the English source it renders. Paired with translates_digest. Written 2026-09-17 for language-culture's Georgian charter; the brief joined 2026-09-18 when the role got one.

translates_digest.description: sha256 of the source's body (frontmatter stripped) at the time of translation; lint reports a translation whose digest no longer matches its source — the translation lags.
